comments.body: RCA (Phase 1 only; no fix landed): The five `test_atomic_completion_close.py` failures are host-harness environment contamination, not a missing `refs/heads/tickets` ref and not a Git 2.55 push/default-branch change. This session inherits `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3` with `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit`, which overrides the user's global `safe.bareRepository=all`. The failing assertions call the test helper `_git(remote, ...)` on a bare fixture remote (`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46`, remote created/pushed in `_ticket_remote` at :102-117), and Git refuses that read with `fatal: cannot use bare repository ... (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')`. Inspection of the failed fixture remotes with `git -c safe.bareRepository=all -C <remote> rev-parse refs/heads/tickets` proves the ref exists. Discriminating experiment: running the same target file with only the injected `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries removed, still using host `git version 2.55.0`, passes: `17 passed in 40.47s`. A minimal Git 2.55 push to a bare remote likewise creates `refs/heads/tickets` when the injected config is absent. CI impact: expected none for Gerrit Verified; `_build-and-test.yml`/`gerrit-verify.yaml` run on `ubuntu-latest`, install Python 3.12/uv, and do not set this Copilot harness `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` override. Disposition: accepted as environment/config; local full-suite pre-flight in this harness may show this cluster red unless `GIT_CONFIG_*` injection is sanitized or bare-remote test helpers opt in to safe bare access. No code fix landed.

RCA COMPLETE — disposition: ACCEPTED (host-environment artifact, no code fix warranted).

Root cause: the injected Copilot/Git environment sets GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3 with KEY_0=safe.bareRepository=explicit (also credential.interactive=never, core.fsmonitor=""). The test helper reads the bare fixture remotes via `git -C <tickets-remote.git> ...`; with safe.bareRepository=explicit git REFUSES to operate on a bare repo discovered via -C, yielding exit 128 (the refs/heads/tickets ref actually exists). Not git 2.55.0 behavior, not origin/main breakage.

Proof: with the injected GIT_CONFIG_* removed, the same host+git gives `17 passed`. Neutralizing just the one key also fixes it:
  env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=4 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_3=safe.bareRepository GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_3=all PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test  → 17 passed

CI impact: NONE. Gerrit `Verified` runs on ubuntu-latest without this injected env, so the cluster is green in CI.

Guidance for the janitor epic (78f2): full-suite LOCAL pre-flight on this host must prepend the safe.bareRepository=all override (append as GIT_CONFIG entry #3). This does NOT block landing. No production/test code change required.

DISPOSITION CORRECTED. The two earlier RCA comments get the mechanism roughly right but reach the wrong conclusion -- 'host-environment artifact, no code fix warranted'. That conclusion is contradicted by this project's own recorded policy and by an existing regression oracle that this file simply escaped.

Closed ticket 3476-4472-3407-4246 (embolismic-adverse-dragon) states it verbatim: 'the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. Treat agents dismissing reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.' That ticket converted 13 files off the same construct and added tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py as a held-out guard.

The guard did not catch this one because it pins a hardcoded 3-entry _FIXTURE_NODES allowlist. test_atomic_completion_close.py was added 2026-08-25 by commit 1cb1cdd25aff -- four days AFTER the guard landed and three days BEFORE 3476 closed -- reintroducing the banned construct at five sites. There is no static sweep anywhere (scripts/, Makefile, .pre-commit-config.yaml) that would flag it; scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py covers an unrelated concern.

Two factual corrections to the original report, now reflected in the retitled ticket: the refs/heads/tickets ref EXISTS and resolves fine (git refuses to open the bare repo before any ref lookup), and git 2.55.0 is irrelevant -- safe.bareRepository shipped in git 2.38.0 on 2022-10-03 with exactly these semantics, so the behavior is four years old and there is no version regression to chase.

Title and description rewritten around the actual cause. AC4 deliberately targets the allowlist itself: fixing only the five call sites would leave the same gap that produced this recurrence.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

Five tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` fail locally for any
developer whose git config sets `safe.bareRepository = explicit`. They pass under git's default
(`all`), which is what CI uses, so **CI can never exercise this path**. All five fail identically
— not an assertion, a `CalledProcessError` from the test helper: `Command '['git', '-C',
'.../tickets-remote.git', 'ls-tree', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 128`.

## Root cause

`git` refuses to **discover** a bare repository via `-C` / cwd when `safe.bareRepository=explicit`;
it accepts one named by a top-level `--git-dir`. Exit 128 is a refusal to open the repository at
all, *before* any ref lookup:

```
git -C <bare>  -> fatal: cannot use bare repository '<bare>' (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')
git --git-dir <bare>  -> exit 0
```

The offending helper is `_git` at `test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46`, which hardcodes
`["git", "-C", str(repo), *args]`. The bare remote is built in `_ticket_remote` (:97-117) and read
at **:401, :402, :415, :423, :435, :455, :493, :576** — eight sites across the five failing
tests.

Two claims in the original report are wrong: the `refs/heads/tickets` ref EXISTS (git never gets
as far as looking it up), and git 2.55.0 is a red herring — `safe.bareRepository` shipped in git
2.38.0 with these exact semantics.

## This is a recurrence of a class already fixed

Closed ticket `3476-4472-3407-4246` (`embolismic-adverse-dragon`) records the policy verbatim:
"the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. **Treat agents dismissing reproducible
local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.**" It converted 13 files from
`git -C <bare>` to `git --git-dir <bare>` and added the held-out oracle
`tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py`.

**Why this file escaped the guard:** that oracle pins a **hardcoded allowlist** of 3 fixture nodes
(`_FIXTURE_NODES`). `test_atomic_completion_close.py` was added on 2026-08-25 by commit
`1cb1cdd25aff` — four days *after* the guard landed — and reintroduced the banned construct. There
is no static sweep either, so the guard only checks three files that were already fixed and cannot
fail when a new file reintroduces the defect. **That allowlist is why this is the second
occurrence, and leaving it is why there would be a third.**

## Plan

1. **Point fix.** Add a sibling helper `_bare_git(remote, *args)` that addresses the bare remote
   with a top-level `--git-dir`, and route only the bare-remote call sites through it. `_git` is
   also used on **non-bare** worktrees (`tracker`, `writer`, `tmp_path` for `init`/`clone`), so a
   blanket `-C` -> `--git-dir` swap is wrong. This is the shape ticket 3476 already established in
   the integration fixtures (`_bare_git` beside `_git`).
2. **Close the oracle gap with a static sweep, in the repo's established gate idiom.** Add
   `scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py` alongside `check_raw_git_writes.py` and
   `check_wall_clock_asserts.py`, wired into `make lint`, carrying
   `# mechanism-ok: ci_gate scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py — <reason>` in its opening
   lines, since the mechanism-delta ratchet fails on any new gate script without one. It AST-sweeps
   every `tests/**/*.py` and, per module, derives the identifiers bound to a bare repository:
   - the last path operand after a `--bare` token (`git init --bare <dir>`, and
     `git clone --bare <src> <dst>`, whose *source* must not be marked);
   - the directory the call runs in when the flag takes no operand (`_git(remote, "init", "-q",
     "--bare")`, the shape the already-fixed integration fixtures use);
   - a name bound by a bare-repository factory: a `bare`-named creator taking only paths
     (`init_bare_remote(remote)`), or a same-module helper that creates a bare repository **and
     returns it** — tracked by return POSITION (`return remote, writer` marks only the first
     element; a helper returning the *worktree* marks nothing) and applied to the **caller's
     binding name**, so a rename (`origin, scribe = _ticket_remote(...)`) is covered;
   - the **argument passed at a parameter position** that the callee marks bare in its own body,
     which is what covers `_publish_ticket_store(repo, remote)` by dataflow rather than by the
     caller happening to spell the name the same way.
   Marking is otherwise module-scoped by identifier, which covers the same flows a second way.
   Then flag any `-C` invocation targeting a marked name — direct, or through a module-local helper
   that forwards its first parameter to `-C`. Two calls are **exempt**: one carrying the inline
   `-c safe.bareRepository=all` opt-in, the deliberate escape ticket 3476 preserved in
   `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py` (it passes under the strict config today);
   and the **creating** call, since `git -C <dir> init --bare` runs before `<dir>` is a repository.
3. **Retire the allowlist.** Delete `_FIXTURE_NODES` from
   `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py`; it becomes the oracle
   for the sweep — asserting the checker reports nothing tree-wide, self-testing the detector on
   synthetic offending / renamed-binding / escaped modules so it cannot rot into a tautology, and
   pinning the git behaviour the rule encodes (`-C` on a bare repo exits 128 naming
   `safe.bareRepository`; `--git-dir` exits 0).
4. Fix every site the sweep flags, so `make lint` is green on landing: 12 sites in 2 files — 8 in
   the file under fix and 4 in `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`, whose
   `test_fresh_clone_json_exposes_allocation_without_a_policy_verdict` and
   `test_invalid_configured_branch_cleans_only_its_temporary_child` fail under the strict config
   today for exactly the same reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file setting safe.bareRepository=explicit> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` exits 0 with 17 passed (today: 5 failed, 12 passed).
- [ ] The same file still passes under default git config (17 passed), and the full `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle` run still passes.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` passes under the strict config too (today: 2 failed, 5 passed) and under the default config.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py` exits 0 on the fixed tree and is run by `make lint`; reintroducing the `git -C <bare-repo>` construct anywhere under `tests/` makes it exit non-zero. Demonstrated by temporarily reverting one call site, observing the guard go RED, and restoring it.
- [ ] The guard's coverage is derived from the tree, not from a hand-maintained file allowlist: `_FIXTURE_NODES` is gone, and a new bare-fixture test using `git -C <bare>` fails the gate with no registration step.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, including the module-size, complexity and mechanism-delta ratchets, with the new gate justified by an inline `# mechanism-ok: ci_gate ...` marker rather than a hand-edited baseline.

## Testing

- RED first: `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$STRICT GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 python -m pytest <file> -q` must show `5 failed, 12 passed` before the fix and `17 passed` after, and `2 failed, 5 passed` -> `7 passed` for `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- Default-config runs of both files, plus `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle -q`.
- Guard: `python scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py` and `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py -q`, plus a mutation run with one call site reverted to `_git(remote, ...)` proving the gate goes RED.
- Ratchets: `make lint` (module-size, complexity, mechanism-delta) and `make typecheck`.
